diagnostic_evidence.quote: Starting from any initialization $\w_0$, for any stationary point $\bar{\w}$ attained by \mkl, we have that $\bar{\w} \in \mathcal{B}_r(\ws)$

Now, we can repeat the above analysis recursively for every corresponding $\w_C$ and $\tilde{\w}$ in the landscape and so now $\theta_j$ is a function of $\tilde{\w}$ as well as is represented in the theorem statement.

issues.failure_explanation: Stationarity at $\bar w$ means $\sum_i p_i(\bar w)\nabla f_i(\bar w)=0$, but the proof substitutes probabilities evaluated at a different, remote point $\w_C=C\bar w$ (chosen so outliers have the lowest loss there). The selection probabilities depend on the loss ranking at the evaluation point, so $p_i(\w_C)\neq p_i(\bar w)$ in general, and the resulting weighted-mean expression and all later bounds do not constrain actual MKL stationary points; at best they analyze a virtual fixed point with adversarially frozen weights, and no self-consistency (that the ranking at the solution reproduces the assumed weights) is verified. Two further gaps: the derived bound $\|\bar w-\ws\|\le\|\widetilde w-\ws\|/\cos\theta_j\ge\|\widetilde w-\ws\|$ does not place $\bar w$ inside $\mathcal B_r(\ws)$ (the $l_m$–$l_M$ crossing used is not the binding one for the region where all outliers outrank all clean samples), and the elimination of every other ordering is only asserted recursively. The sufficient condition is also written in terms of $\theta_{M,\bar w}$, a property of the unknown stationary point.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the frozen-weight analysis with a rigorous region-by-region fixed-point argument: in each loss-ordering region solve the genuine stationarity equation with probabilities evaluated at the candidate point, and show that under a condition on problem data (not on the unknown $\bar w$) no self-consistent solution exists outside $\mathcal B_r(\ws)$.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central global landscape guarantee — from any initialization every stationary point lies in the good ball — is unsupported. This also underlies the scalar-case conclusions drawn from Condition cond:1, the 'very strong worst-case guarantee' prose, and the 'Effect of $\kappa$/$\gamma$' paragraphs. Theorem theorem:relativebounds is only conditional on $\wsm\in\mathcal B_r(\ws)$, so its advertised force loses the justification that attained solutions are ever in the ball.
issues.title: Lemma lemma:vector proof computes stationary points with selection probabilities evaluated at the wrong point; global in-ball guarantee unproven
issues.why_classification: This is the paper's main global guarantee; the source contains no valid argument for it and any repair requires a new proof architecture (self-consistent fixed-point/landscape analysis) or a major change of the guarantee, so it is serious even though no labelled result formally depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For the sake of simplicity, we will assume that $\norm{\nabla f_i(\bs{w})} \leq G ~\forall~i\in \mathbb{O}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a hypothesis lower-bounding the aggregate outlier influence, e.g. $\|\sum_{j\in\mathbb O}\nabla f_j(\wsgd)\|\ge \epsilon n g$ for some $g>0$ (ruling out gradient cancellation), and replace $G$ by that lower bound in the lemma; the existing combination with lemma:m2lboundstrongconvexity then yields theorem:relativebounds in the same form for the restricted outlier regime.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lemma:sgdbound is false as stated; Theorem theorem:relativebounds (every in-ball MKL stationary point is closer to $\ws$ than SGD by the factor $\alpha<1$) inherits the defect and fails in cancelling-outlier instances, where $\|\wsgd-\ws\|=0$ while the in-ball MKL stationary point is bounded away from $\ws$. The setup prose 'now vanilla SGD on the entire loss function will {\em not} converge to $\ws$' is the same unsupported assertion.
issues.title: Lemma lemma:sgdbound derives a lower bound on SGD's error from upper bounds; false without a lower bound on outlier gradient influence
issues.why_classification: A contained repair exists — one new restrictive hypothesis plus the paper's own short combination argument — leaving a recognizably comparable comparison theorem, but it narrows the advertised outlier regime and the current proof cannot be fixed locally: more than minor, not a rebuild.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: it is possible that \mkl~gets stuck at any one of the many local minimas that exist close to the outlier center $w_B$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof's key step bounds the total outlier selection probability by $\sum_{i\in\mathbb O}p_i(\wsm)\le\epsilon^k$, which holds only when every outlier has higher loss than every clean sample at $\wsm$, i.e. $\wsm\in\mathcal B_r(\ws)$. The statement omits this hypothesis and claims the bound for any stationary point. Stationary points outside the ball exist — the paper itself describes MKL getting stuck at local minima close to the outlier center $w_B$ when Condition 1 fails — and for them $\|\wsm-\ws\|$ is $\Theta(\delta)$, violating the claimed $O(\epsilon^k)$ bound.

failure_location.quote: Let $\wsm$ be any first order stationary point attained by \mkl.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis $\wsm\in\mathcal B_r(\ws)$ (equivalently, that all outliers rank below all clean samples at $\wsm$); the given proof then goes through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma is false as stated. Its only downstream use is in Theorem theorem:relativebounds, whose own statement already supplies the missing hypothesis ('for any $\wsm \in \mathcal{B}_r(\ws)$'), so no labelled downstream result is invalidated by this root.
issues.title: Lemma lemma:m2lboundstrongconvexity quantifies over all stationary points but its proof requires the in-ball hypothesis
issues.why_classification: A short, strictly local repair (one added hypothesis that matches exactly how the lemma is used in theorem:relativebounds); method, conclusion, and advertised scope all survive: minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: m= m(\wsm)\footnote{Note that strong convexity holds since we are only considering the set of good samples}

issues.failure_explanation: The proof derives $m(\wsm)\,\|\wsm-\ws\|\le\epsilon^k G$, where $m(\wsm)$ is the secant/strong-convexity constant of the good-sample weighted sum $\sum_{i\notin O}p_i(\wsm)\nabla f_i(\wsm)$ at $\wsm$. The statement instead uses $\lambda=\min_w\lambda_w$ with $\lambda_w$ the Lemma lemma:sc constants of the full surrogate (all samples). Since the full surrogate equals the good part plus a convex outlier part, $\lambda_w\ge m(w)$ for every $w$, so $\lambda=\min_w\lambda_w$ need not satisfy $\lambda\le m(\wsm)$ — the substitution goes the wrong way and is justified nowhere (the text only offers the 'naive' identity $\lambda_w=\min_i p_i(w)\lambda$). A $\lambda$ larger than the valid constant makes the stated bound stronger than what is proved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define $\lambda$ directly as a uniform lower bound on the good-part secant constants $m(w)$ — positivity follows from the source's own observation that $\min_i p_i(w)\ge 1/n^k>0$ together with Assumption 2 — and use that $\lambda$ in both the lemma and theorem:relativebounds.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit constant in lemma:m2lboundstrongconvexity, and hence the factor $\alpha(\epsilon,L,k,\lambda)=(1-\epsilon)L\epsilon^{k-1}/\lambda$ in theorem:relativebounds, is not the constant the analysis yields; the quantitative comparison bound is unsupported as written.
issues.title: Lemma lemma:m2lboundstrongconvexity states the bound with lambda from eq:lambdasc but its proof establishes a different constant
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local definitional correction using positivity already argued in the source; the form and rates of all claims are unchanged: minor.

Exact convergence with $k\ge n\epsilon+1$ holds only for the without-replacement variant (every $k$-set then contains a clean sample, driving in-ball outlier probability to 0) and only if iterates remain in the ball — conditions the claim does not state and that contradict the declared model. failure_location.quote: To ensure consistency, i.e. $\norm{\wsm -\ws} \rightarrow 0$, we require that $k \geq n\epsilon + 1$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the claim to the supported statement: with-replacement MKL converges to a neighborhood of radius $O(\epsilon^k G/\lambda)$ (shrinking with $k$), and exact convergence to $\ws$ is possible only for the without-replacement variant with $k>\epsilon n$ and iterates confined to $\mathcal B_r(\ws)$.
issues.overall_effect: A conclusion-section guarantee of exact consistency (with known $\epsilon$, the right $k$, and smart initialization) that the formal results do not support and that is false for the declared sampling model; it misstates what the analyzed algorithm can achieve and contradicts the paper's own neighborhood bound.

issues.why_classification: The consistency promise must be withdrawn or re-scoped to a different sampling variant plus ball conditions — a limited weakening of an advertised guarantee with no dependents, while the paper's neighborhood-convergence results survive: moderate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: And thus we use Lemma \ref{lemma:m2lboundstrongconvexity} in conjunction with \ref{lemma:sgdbound}.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper defines only Assumptions 1-3 (plus an unnumbered prose bound $\|\nabla f_i\|\le G$ for outliers); assumptions N1, N2, A4, A5 and the symbols $N, N'$ are never defined, so the lemma's hypotheses — hence its validity — are undetermined as written. diagnostic_evidence.quote:
If  we are at the same point $\bs{w_t}$ for both SGD and MKL-SGD and $p_i(\bs{w_t})< \dfrac{1}{N}$ for $i \in \mathbb{O}$, we have
$R_t^{(SGD)}>R_t^{(MKL)}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds MKL-2's outlier terms $\sum_{i>|\mathcal G|}\frac{2(n-i)}{n(n-1)}(f_i(\wg)-f_i(\bs{w_t}))$ by the SGD expression $\frac1n\sum_{i>|\mathcal G|}(f_i(\wg)-f_i(\bs{w_t}))$ via $\frac{2(n-i)}{n(n-1)}\le\frac1n$; this term-by-term comparison requires $f_i(\wg)-f_i(\bs{w_t})\ge0$ for outliers, which no hypothesis implies (the condition $\sup_{i\in\mathcal G}f_i(\bs{w_t})\le\inf_{j\in\mathbb O}f_j(\bs{w_t})$ does not compare $f_j(\bs{w_t})$ with $f_j(\wg)$). When $f_j(\bs{w_t})>f_j(\wg)$ the inequality reverses and the conclusion fails: e.g. $n=4$, good losses $w^2$ ($\wg=0$), two outliers $(w-10)^2$, at $\bs{w_t}=-1$ all hypotheses hold ($|\mathcal G|=n/2$; good losses $1\le121$; good gradients at $\wg$ vanish so the noise-level condition holds) but the outlier bracket equals $100-121=-21<0$ with MKL weights below uniform, yielding $R_t^{(MKL_2)}>R_t^{(SGD)}$ for small $\eta_t$. The same sign error underlies the main-text claim that $R_t^{(SGD)}>R_t^{(MKL)}$ whenever $p_i(\bs{w_t})<1/N$ for outliers.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a hypothesis forcing the outlier brackets nonnegative, e.g. $f_j(\bs{w_t})\le f_j(\wg)$ for all $j\in\mathbb O$ (or otherwise control the negative part), and restate the comparison under the strengthened conditions; the remainder of the proof then goes through.
issues.overall_effect: The corollary's sufficient conditions do not suffice; the advertised conclusion — MKL-2 one-step-dominates SGD even when more than half the data is corrupted — is false as stated, as is the matching main-text comparison built on eq:expressR.
issues.title: Corollary cor:added-1's claim that MKL-2 dominates SGD fails because outlier loss-difference terms can be negative
issues.why_classification: A contained fix exists (an extra, restrictive hypothesis) leaving a formally comparable sufficient condition, but it substantially narrows the result's scope and the proof's key comparison step is invalid as written: moderate.
